blocks.prompt: 1. Find equation of the altitude of triangle \(XYZ\) from vertex \(X(1, 3)\), \(Y(5, 7)\) and \(Z(-3, 9)\).
blocks.explanation:
Is sawal mein triangle \(XYZ\) ke vertices diye hain: \(X(1, 3)\), \(Y(5, 7)\), \(Z(-3, 9)\). Kitab ka jumla thora ulajh gaya hai, lekin matlab yeh hai ke vertex \(X\) se altitude ki equation chahiye.
Altitude woh line hai jo vertex se guzre aur samne wali side par perpendicular ho; \(X\) ke samne side \(YZ\) hai.
Is liye do cheezein chahiye: ek point (\(X\)) aur ek slope (\(YZ\) par perpendicular).
Plan: pehle \(YZ\) ki slope, phir perpendicular slope \(m_1m_2 = -1\) se, aur aakhir mein point-slope form.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(X(1, 3)\), \(Y(5, 7)\), \(Z(-3, 9)\).
Maloom karna: \(X\) se altitude ki equation.
Tareeqa: \(X\) se altitude \(\overline{YZ}\) par perpendicular hai aur \(X\) se guzarta hai; point aur slope maloom hon to point-slope form sab se munasib hai.

\(\overline{YZ}\) ki slope
\[m_{YZ} = \dfrac{9 - 7}{-3 - 5} = \dfrac{2}{-8} = -\dfrac{1}{4}\]
Kyun: side ke dono siron se slope \(= \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}\). Yahan \(Y\) pehla aur \(Z\) doosra point liya.
Dhyan dein: upar aur neeche dono jagah points ki tarteeb ek hi rakhein, warna sign ulta ho jayega.

Altitude ki slope
\[m = \dfrac{-1}{m_{YZ}} = \dfrac{-1}{-\frac{1}{4}} = 4\]
Kyun: perpendicular lines ki slopes ka product \(-1\) hota hai, is liye slope ulti (reciprocal) aur sign badla hua: \(-\frac{1}{4}\) se \(4\).

\(X(1, 3)\) se equation
\[y - 3 = 4(x - 1)\]
\[y - 3 = 4x - 4\]
\[4x - y - 1 = 0\]
Kyun: point-slope form \(y - y_1 = m(x - x_1)\) mein \(X\) aur \(m = 4\) rakhe, phir sab terms ek taraf le aaye taake general form ban jaye.

Tasdeeq:
\(X(1, 3)\) rakhein: \(4 - 3 - 1 = 0\), yani line \(X\) se guzarti hai. Line ki slope \(4\) hai aur \(4 \times \left(-\frac{1}{4}\right) = -1\), yani yeh \(YZ\) par perpendicular hai. Jawab answer key (number 2) se milta hai.
